messages.subject: Basic question about using R for data coding
messages.subject_clean: Basic question about using R for data coding
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to make the transition from using a WYSIWYG spreadsheet/database program (e.g., OpenOffice Calc) to R for actually coding my data. What I'd like to be able to do is load my data into R and have it provide an interface for coding each token according to a single particular variable. So, for instance, if I'm working with English data about complementizer usage, I would like to load my data and then have each token presented individually to code for one variable at a time--e.g., presence/absence of complementizer.

I realize this is probably beyond basic in R, but any suggestions would help.

Thanks,
Chad

messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] Basic question about using R for data coding
messages.body_plain:
Hi

Well, that type of stuff is indeed possible. On the very simplest of
all levels, you can use edit(). An intermediate approach would be to
write a script that outputs the concordance line or something, asks
you for a variable value (maybe with select.list so you have a window,
or with menu), and then the level you enter will be added to the
vector offered as a choice. If you want to do this cooler, you can
have R guess what the most likely level is (based on some similarity
measure) and have that be the default suggestion; I wrote something
like in Perl once for corpus annotation. A nicer approach would of
course involve writing a little thing that does everything in tcltk
...

Cheers,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries
